text: Hello, dinosaur explorers! Let us meet twelve amazing prehistoric animals. Tap a picture to hear its name. The sound button plays an imagined animal call.
Tyrannosaurus rex walked on two strong legs. Its arms were small. Can you find them?
Triceratops had three horns and a wide frill. Can you count the horns? One, two, three!
Stegosaurus had tall plates along its back and spikes on its tail. Point to a plate, then a spike.
Brachiosaurus had a long neck. Its front legs were longer than its back legs. Imagine reaching high into a leafy tree.
Diplodocus had a long neck and a very long, slender tail. Follow the tail with your finger. Where does it end?
Ankylosaurus wore bony armour. Its tail ended in a heavy club. Can you spot the club in the picture?
Brontosaurus was a giant plant eater with a long neck and sturdy legs. Imagine its slow steps through the ferns.
Spinosaurus had a tall sail on its back and a long snout. It ate fish. Can you trace the shape of its sail?
Pteranodon was a flying reptile, not a dinosaur. It had a long beak and wide wings. Spread your arms like wings!
Quetzalcoatlus was another flying reptile. It had a long neck and an enormous wingspan. Imagine the shadow of those wings.
Parasaurolophus had a long curved crest on its head. Scientists think its crest may have helped it make sounds. What do you imagine?
Velociraptor was much smaller than the giants in this book. It had feathers. Look for the feathers on its arms and tail.
Which animal would you like to meet again? Some lived millions of years apart. Their real voices are a mystery, so our sounds are made for imagination.

Milo wanted to visit his friend across the stream. The old stepping stones were under water. We need a little bridge, he said.
First, the builders looked carefully. They chose firm ground on both banks. Milo drew a bridge with a wide path and strong sides.
The orange digger scooped a little earth. Scoop, lift, and set it down. The workers made a steady place for each end of the bridge.
The blue truck brought stones. Its bed lifted slowly. The stones tumbled into a tidy pile. That is enough, said Milo.
The crane lifted a strong beam. Everyone stood clear. Up slowly, across carefully, and down gently. The beam joined the two banks.
The builders added boards and sturdy rails. They checked for wobbles and sharp edges. A smooth path helps wheels and little feet.
A grown-up builder checked the finished bridge. Strong, steady, and ready! Milo waited for the all-clear, then walked across with his friend.
Now friends could visit in muddy weather. A little wagon rolled across too. Milo waved to the builders. We made a way for everyone!
Ari and Pip packed for a pretend moon adventure. Helmets, gloves, and a picnic! Their rocket waited under the stars. Where shall we go first?
Ari checked the seat belts. Pip checked the map. Three, two, one, lift off! Their pretend rocket rose into the sparkling night.
Through the window, Earth looked blue and white. That is our home, said Ari. Pip drew a little heart beside it on the map.
They landed gently. The real moon has no air to breathe, so astronauts need spacesuits. Ari and Pip kept their pretend helmets closed.
Moon gravity is weaker than Earth's. Ari imagined a long slow hop. Hop, pause, look! Pip followed a trail of round footprints.
They found a crater, a big hollow in the ground. Space rocks made many moon craters. Ari looked from a safe spot and sketched its shape.
Inside the rocket, Ari sent a message home. We saw craters and imagined moon hops! Pip saved their pictures. Now it was time to return.
Their pretend mission ended with a picnic at home. The moon shone above them. Next time, said Ari, let us imagine another adventure.
Lila the fairy found a flower with a drooping head. Hello, little flower, she whispered. What would help you feel better today?
Lila touched the soil gently. It felt dry. She fetched her little watering can. Plants need water, but not a great big flood.
Drip, drop, drip. Lila poured a little water around the roots. A ladybird rested on a leaf and watched the droplets shine.
A fallen leaf was covering the small plant. Lila moved it aside. Now the green leaves could reach toward the warm sunshine.
Lila waited. She watched the clouds and listened to the garden. Growing takes time. She could care for the flower without hurrying it.
On another morning, the flower stood taller. A butterfly fluttered by. It settled for a moment, then danced away between the leaves.
Look! A new little bud had appeared. Lila smiled. Water, light, and patient care had helped the garden grow. What a lovely surprise.
Lila left room for all her garden visitors. The flower, the butterfly, and the tiny ladybird each belonged. Who might visit your garden?
Princess Nora found a star-shaped lantern in the courtyard. It had rolled away from the evening parade. Someone must be looking for you, she said.
Nora asked the gardener. Have you seen this star? The gardener shook her head, then pointed toward the busy village square. Let us ask together.
A little golden ribbon lay on the path. It matched the lantern's ribbon. Nora followed it carefully, keeping the lantern safe in both hands.
Beside the bakery, a basket had tipped over. Nora stopped to help gather the wrapped rolls. Thank you, said the baker. Kindness is never a detour.
In the square, a child was searching beside the parade cart. My star is missing, he said. Nora knelt down. Is this the one you made?
That is my star! The child smiled. Nora helped tie its ribbon onto the cart. Together they checked that the knot was secure.
Walk with us, said the child. Nora joined the parade. There were big lanterns and tiny lanterns, each made by someone in the village.
The lanterns glowed as evening fell. Nora had not found a real star from the sky. She had found a chance to help, and new friends to share the light.
Mira the mermaid spotted a shell with rainbow colours. It rested in the sand beside a swaying sea plant. What a beautiful little home, she said.
Mira looked closely before touching it. A tiny claw peeked out. Someone was already living inside! The shell belonged to a little hermit crab.
The little crab wanted to reach a sheltered rock. But a loose piece of litter lay across the sand. Mira knew litter did not belong in the sea.
Mira carefully lifted the loose litter into her basket. She would take it to the shore for proper disposal. Now the sandy path was clear.
Mira swam beside the crab. She did not hurry him or carry his shell away. Slow was a good speed for such small legs.
At last, the crab reached a calm spot beside the rock. Little fish drifted past. Mira waved gently and gave her new neighbour plenty of room.
Mira left the rainbow shell with its owner. The best treasure was a living sea to care for, full of creatures with homes of their own.
Mira swam home with her basket of litter. Next time she saw a pretty shell, she would look closely first. What might you notice by the sea?
